name: Tzatziki
why: A cold garlic and cucumber sauce that turns plain roast chicken into a meal. Uses two things you have too much of.

steps.text: Grate half a cucumber using the grating blade on your slicer.
steps.look: Skin on is fine and adds colour. You want shreds, not slices.

steps.text: Squeeze the water out of the grated cucumber. Put it in a fistful of paper towel and wring it hard over the sink.
steps.look: You will be surprised how much comes out, easily a few tablespoons. Keep squeezing until it stops dripping.
steps.warn: This is the entire difference between tzatziki and a watery mess. Cucumber is about 96% water and all of it ends up in the yogurt if you skip this. Do not skip it.

steps.text: Grate or finely chop 1 garlic clove and mix everything: 200 g yogurt, the squeezed cucumber, the garlic, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1/2 tsp kosher salt.
steps.look: One clove is enough. Raw garlic gets stronger as it sits, so what tastes mild now will be assertive tomorrow.

steps.text: Chill 30 minutes before eating if you can. Keeps 4 days.
steps.look: It tastes flat straight after mixing and comes together as it sits.About 11 g of protein in the batch, but that is not the point. It is a sauce, and it makes the leg quarters and the roast into something you actually want to eat again on day three.
